one_line_contribution: A paired, pre-registered ALFWorld measurement of how much a procedural memory bank is still worth once a reflective prompt optimizer has written the instruction from the identical training episodes (the 'residual' g(I_P)), plus a task-disjoint, no-memory-accuracy-matched instruction I'_match intended to separate episode-specific absorption from distribution-level absorption.
closest_prior_work: ExpeL (2308.10144) and EvoAgentBench (2607.05202), and ExpeL is the more dangerous of the two because the proposal quotes it correctly against itself. I verified ExpeL's ALFWorld ablation: full 59, retrieve-only 55, insights-only 50. The proposal's estimand g(I) = acc(I x B) - acc(I x M0) is, in ExpeL's own table, 59 - 50 = 9 points: the residual value of the retrieval container measured at an already-written insights instruction built from the same training pool. So the joint cell the proposal calls unpublished is published, and its published value is about +9pt, not about 0. The entire paper is a bet that swapping ExpeL's extraction routine for a search-based optimizer closes a 9-point gap. That bet is placed with a 350-rollout GEPA-lite budget on 300 training games (one full sweep plus 50 rollouts, i.e. roughly one mutation actually evaluated) and a local 27B/32B reflector, which is the weakest possible version of the very mechanism the novelty rests on. EvoAgentBench compounds this: it already puts a bank method and GEPA on a shared trajectory pool with a held-out split explicitly constructed so test tasks do not duplicate training instances, which is already a provenance-controlled instruction-vs-bank comparison. The proposal's genuine increment over these two is narrow: the joint cell measured with per-instruction re-tuned k, and the disjoint-pool level-matched arm. That is a delta on a conceded result, and the proposal says so itself ('Novelty is capped by the concessions above').
strongest_objection: The confirmatory family is arithmetically unlikely to declare anything, and the proposal proves this in its own text. E (equivalence within +/-3pt) is declarable only when |g-hat(I_P)| <= 0.9pt, because SE(g) ~ 1.25pt at n=1800 with DEFF 1.4. D is thresholded at 3pt but powered at ~4pt, so 'a true 3pt difference passes about half the time' (their Risk Factor 3). The prior evidence the proposal itself assembles - ExpeL's ~9pt analogous residual, this program's own +0.6 to +2.4pt, MemHarness's raw-injection gap - all point to a true residual in the 1-4pt band, which is exactly the band where E cannot be declared and superiority cannot be claimed either. The modal outcome of row 2 crossed with row 3 is therefore 'bounded residual, D indeterminate': two confidence intervals and no claim, dressed as a pre-registered reading. Second, and independent of power, row 3 does not identify what it claims. I'_match is a mid-run snapshot of an optimizer run on P'_train, titrated only on no-memory S_dev accuracy. Matching accuracy does not match instruction maturity, specificity, or length, and the design token-matches I0_pad to I_P but never token- or budget-matches I'_match to I_P. A larger g at I'_match is therefore fully explained by 'I' is an earlier, thinner, less specific instruction that leaves more for the bank to say' - a rival the proposal never names and never arms. Since D is the one arm carrying the word 'episode-specific' in the title, an identification hole there is not a secondary blemish. Third, the bank B is an insight/strategy bank (ExpeL-style INSIGHT/PROCEDURE/OUTCOME or ReasoningBank-style strategies), not a raw-trajectory retrieval bank, and ExpeL found retrieval (55) beat insights (50) on ALFWorld specifically because ALFWorld rewards concrete action sequences. The design therefore measures the residual of the container ALFWorld is known to reward less, which biases the whole study toward the null it hopes to declare.
what_would_fix_it: (1) Change the primary estimand. Make the retention ratio R = g(I_P)/g(I0*) with a cluster-bootstrap CI the confirmatory quantity instead of a TOST that only fires below 0.9pt; R is always declarable, is the quantity Experience Distillation reports, and answers the title's question in the form readers want. If the TOST is kept, either raise rows 2-3 to n >= 3000 (the ~700 reserve is not enough) or pre-justify a +/-5pt margin from a stated decision-theoretic cost rather than picking 3. (2) Add row 3b: an early snapshot of I_P itself, from the SAME episodes, titrated to the same no-memory level and matched on rollout budget and token count to I'_match. Without it, D confounds episode provenance with optimizer maturity, and D is the title. (3) Add a raw-trajectory demonstration-retrieval bank at I_P (see missing_baseline) so the null is not declared on the weaker container. (4) Give the optimizer a budget that makes 'search-based reflective optimizer' true: 350 rollouts over 300 games is one sweep plus 50, and calling coverage '100% by construction' is definitional, not empirical. Several thousand rollouts, or a candidate-count-per-generation table, or stop claiming search is the differentiator from AutoManual/AutoGuide. (5) Move official valid_unseen from Tier 1 into Tier 0. A claim about ALFWorld memory that never touches the split every cited memory paper reports on, and that sits behind contingency cuts, will not be read as on the published axis. (6) Close collision obligation (1) and read 2608.14036 before freezing, not after.
missing_baseline: A raw-trajectory / demonstration-retrieval memory bank at I_P, k- and token-matched to B. Every arm in the grid uses a distilled insight-or-strategy bank, but ExpeL's ALFWorld ablation (which the proposal quotes) shows retrieve-only 55 versus insights-only 50, i.e. the trajectory container is the stronger one in exactly this environment, and MIPROv2 - also cited - frames the whole instruction-versus-demonstration decomposition around demonstrations, not distilled prose. Declaring 'the optimized instruction absorbed the bank' after testing only the prose-shaped bank tests the arm most similar to the instruction and is close to circular; a reviewer will read the null as an artifact of container choice. Second omission, equally demandable: a same-episode, budget- and level-matched early snapshot of I_P as the comparator for I'_match, so that D contrasts episode provenance rather than optimizer maturity. Third, minor: no scaffold-plus-random-instruction control distinguishes 'an optimized instruction' from 'any long task-specific instruction'; I0_pad pads with task-neutral prose only.
preprint_collision: The check is unusually honest for this venue and concedes six lines of prior work by name, which is credit due. It is also, by its own text, incomplete: obligation (1) - the provenance / held-out-episode crossover search - was run once, found nothing, and is called 'not sufficient'; two 2026 IDs are cited unread; and the appendix of 2608.14036 is deferred. By the standard that an unsearched claim of novelty is a weakness, this one is partly self-reported as unestablished. I ran six searches. VERIFIED AS REAL AND AS DESCRIBED: 2308.10144 ExpeL, and its ALFWorld ablation numbers 59 / 55 / 50 (arxiv.org/abs/2308.10144); 2604.14585 'Prompt Optimization Is a Coin Flip: Diagnosing When It Helps in Compound AI Systems', ICML 2026 workshop, 49% of runs below zero-shot confirmed (arxiv.org/abs/2604.14585); 2607.28272 MemHarness, ALFWorld raw injection 70.1 and RL baseline 76.4 both confirmed (arxiv.org/abs/2607.28272); 2606.29914 MemDelta exists (arxiv.org/abs/2606.29914) but its one-variable flip is demonstrated on LongMemEval-S, not on ALFWorld, so it supports the methodology point and not the environment choice; 2511.21730 exists as 'A Benchmark for Procedural Memory Retrieval in Language Agents' (arxiv.org/abs/2511.21730); 2608.14036 exists as 'Demystifying Agent Skills: Why They Work - Until They Don't' (arxiv.org/html/2608.14036v1). PARTIALLY VERIFIED: 2607.05202 EvoAgentBench exists (arxiv.org/abs/2607.05202, 6 Jul 2026, four domains, ability graphs, held-out tasks that do not duplicate training instances), but the returned description gives 1,006 train / 367 test tasks, and I could not confirm the proposal's '528/267 trajectories on Qwen3.5-27B' or the ReasoningBank +3.6 / GEPA +1.2 figures; the authors should cite the exact table. NO DIRECT COLLISION FOUND on the surviving contribution as stated (residual of a bank at a search-optimized same-episode instruction, with a disjoint-episode level-matched control) - the searches surfaced no paper making that claim. NEW ADJACENT ITEMS THE PROPOSAL DOES NOT CITE, all surfaced by these searches: arxiv.org/html/2609.00549 'Skill Following: Evaluating Actual Skill Use in Retrieval-Enabled LLM Agents' (Sep 2026), which collides directly with rival (e)'s instrument - the item-following rate f(I) is that paper's estimand, and it must now be cited and its metric adopted or distinguished; arxiv.org/abs/2606.00619 MemPro (memory pipeline as an evolvable program, i.e. optimizer applied to the memory side); arxiv.org/abs/2606.23127 'Managing Procedural Memory in LLM Agents' / AFTER, which holds task-skill annotations fixed to separate skill quality from retrieval quality; arxiv.org/html/2608.09096 'Evo-Bench: Can Language Models Improve Agent Harness?'; arxiv.org/pdf/2603.21520 'Generalizable Self-Evolving Memory for Automatic Prompt Optimization'. None of these is a clean scoop, so the collision check does not sink the paper - but the residual novelty after ExpeL's own 9-point joint-cell number and EvoAgentBench's shared-trajectory table is thin enough that 2609.00549 and 2608.14036 must be read before any freeze; if 2608.14036's appendix contains the token-matched compiled-block comparison the proposal suspects, the contribution shrinks to the ALFWorld measurement with its controls, which is the outcome the proposal already anticipates in writing.
